params.Drive: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.
params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack.
params.Cut: Increasing this parameter cuts high frequencies in the negative feedback loop, which can mellow out the overall treble response.
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack.
params.Presence: Boosts upper mid and high frequencies in the power amp, resulting in additional punch and bite.
params.Level: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.
params.Master: Controls the Master Volume of the amplifier.
params.Sag: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.
params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.
params.Ripple: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.
params.Bias: Adjusts the bias of the tubes in the power amp, causing a change in tonality and the distortion characteristic.
params.Bias X: Determines how the power amp tubes’ voicing reacts when pushed hard. Set low for a tighter feel. Set high for more tube compression. This parameter is highly reactive with the Drive and Master settings.

params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.
params.Ripple: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.Drive: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.
params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.
params.Mid: Controls the midrange frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.
params.Presence: Boosts high frequencies in the power amp by modifying the EQ filtering in the power amp's negative feedback loop.
params.Level: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.
params.Master: Controls the master volume of the amplifier. It is located between the preamp and power amp and can be used to get more or less power amp distortion. This amp is VERY loud, and if the Master is cranked, the power amp distortion can be pushed into unpleasant territory.
params.Mid Switch: Changes the value of the treble capacitor in the tone stack. When off, the amp has more of a scooped sound; when on, there is a noticeable upper-mid boost.
params.Jazz Rock: Changes the tonestack's wiring, allowing for two totally separate tonal voices. Jazz is quieter with a lower center frequency for the mids. Rock is louder with a more traditional mid frequency center. Tone controls rarely translate well between the Jazz and Rock settings. If a good sound is achieved in one mode, it is not guaranteed that the same settings in the opposite mode will still sound pleasing.
params.OD Switch: Turns the two-gain-stage tube overdrive circuit on and off. This circuit is located AFTER the tone controls and Drive knob. When the overdrive is turned on it's as if third and fourth gain stages are added to the preamp.
params.OD Drive: Controls the amount of drive or saturation in the overdrive circuit. Since the whole overdrive circuit is after the amp's regular Drive and Tone controls, the range of OD Drive will change based on those earlier knob settings.
params.OD Level: Controls the output level of the overdrive circuit.
params.Bright: Engages one of two different values of bright capacitor, and is more pronounced at lower Drive settings. When Drive is at 10.0, Bright is effectively removed from the amp circuit.
params.FET Boost: Provides a 7-9 dB FET (Field Effect Transistor) boost and tweaks the EQ a bit. The result is similar to placing a FET boost pedal before the amp.
params.PAB: Adds a preamp boost between tube stages 1 and 2, but at the expense of removing the tonestack controls from the circuit.

params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. params.Ripple: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ (40 Hz) of the tonestack.
params.Mid: Controls the midrange frequency EQ of the tonestack.
params.Mid Freq: Sets the frequency controlled by the Mid parameter--220 Hz, 800 Hz, or 3 kHz.
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ (4 kHz) of the tonestack.
params.Level: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.
params.Master: Controls the Master Volume of the amplifier.
params.Sag: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.
params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. params.Mic: Selects the mic pointed at the cabinet. (Guitar and Bass cabs have different sets of mics available.) Mic selection can have as big an impact on your tone as tweaking the Amp's tonestack or even applying an EQ block, so experimentation is key here.
params.Position: Sets the lateral location of the mic in relation to the speaker cone, from center of the speaker to the edge. The "Cap Edge" value may appear in a different location depending on the selected cab.
params.Distance: Sets the distance of the mic from the speaker cone. Choose from 1.00" to 12.00" in 1/4" increments.
params.Angle: Sets the angle of the mic relative to the front of the speaker cabinet. 0 degrees is pointing directly at the speaker, 45 degrees is pointing off-axis.
params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter, letting you remove all audio below a certain frequency. May be useful in removing undesirable low end rumble.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter, letting you remove all audio above a certain frequency. May be useful in removing high end harshness.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the Cab. Use to adjust level against the other side of the Cab block.
params.Pan: Controls the panning of the Cab between the left and right channels. For stereo setups, the Cab block can sound much wider if the two sides are panned opposite of one another ("L 100" and "R 100")
params.Delay: Delays the signal slightly to purposely impart a bit of phase incoherence or at higher values, increase the Cab block's apparent stereo width. A little goes a long way here. When set to "Auto" (all the way left, before 0.0 ms), it approximates the delay through the air when changing the mic Distance parameter.

params.Level: Sets the overall level of the Cab. Use to adjust level against the other side of the Cab block.
params.Pan: Controls the panning of the Cab between the left and right channels. For stereo setups, the Cab block can sound much wider if the two sides are panned opposite of one another ("L 100" and "R 100")
params.Delay: Delays the signal slightly to purposely impart a bit of phase incoherence or at higher values, increase the Cab block's apparent stereo width. A little goes a long way here. When set to "Auto" (all the way left, before 0.0 ms), it approximates the delay through the air when changing the mic Distance parameter.

params.Mic: Selects the mic pointed at the cabinet. (Guitar and Bass cabs have different sets of mics available.) Mic selection can have as big an impact on your tone as tweaking the Amp's tonestack or even applying an EQ block, so experimentation is key here.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the Delay may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).
params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ applied to the repeats, from -15.2 dB (0%) to +8.8 dB (100%).
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ applied to the repeats, from -15.2 dB (0%) to +8.8 dB (100%).
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the Delay may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).
params.ModSpeed: Controls the speed or rate of the modulation applied to the repeats, from 0.05 Hz (0%) to 9.4 Hz (100%).
params.Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the modulation applied to the repeats.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.
params.Depth: Controls the intensity of the tape-style wow & flutter modulation applied to the repeats.
params.Swell: Sets the ramp time for the volume swell applied to the dry signal, from 0.03 seconds (0%) to 1.9 seconds (100%).
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.
params.Threshold: Controls the threshold/sensitivity of the ducking circuit, from -20 dB (0%) to -60 dB (100%). Higher values increase the likelihood of ducking to occur.
params.Ducking: Controls the amount of ducking applied, from none (0%) to -138 dB (100%). Or rather, how far the repeats drop in volume while playing.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the Delay may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).
params.Wow Flt: Controls the amount of wow and flutter, or how much warbly tape sound is heard in the repeats.
params.Drive: Controls how much tape saturation and drive are applied to the repeats.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.Dry Thru: When off, the dry signal is routed through the tape delay's circuitry (even with Mix set to 0%), which can add a bit of warmth and grit. When on, the dry signal bypasses the delay's circuitry.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the Delay may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).
params.Tone: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter to the repeats, from 300 Hz (0%) to 12 kHz (100%).
params.Res: Sets the amount of bit depth reduction applied to the repeats, from full resolution 24-bit (0%) to lo-fi 6-bit crunchiness (100%).
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Adjusts the delay time of tape head 4. Multi-Head has a maximum delay length of 2.5 seconds, with the delay time divided evenly between the 4 tape heads. So if Time is set to 2.000 seconds, tape head 1's time is 500 ms (2000 / 4 = 500). When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats for all four tape heads. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the Delay may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).
params.Heads 1-2: Selects whether tape heads 1 and/or 2 are on or off.
params.Heads 3-4: Selects whether tape heads 3 and/or 4 are on or off.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.
params.Offset: Offsets the left repeat in relation to the right repeat. Normally leave this at 50% unless you want your ping pong repeats to shuffle a bit.
params.Spread: Controls the apparent stereo width of the repeats between the left and right channels.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Time: Determines the length of audio captured before playing it backwards. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of reverse delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one reverse repeat is heard; at 100%, the reversed audio repeats forever.
params.ModSpeed: Controls the speed or rate of pitch modulation applied to the signal BEFORE it's sent into the delay circuit; ModSpeed is not applied to the repeats themselves. Therefore, you can capture your playing with a slow modulation setting, and layer playing with fast modulation on top of it.
params.Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of pitch modulation applied to the signal BEFORE it's sent into the delay circuit. Therefore, you can capture your playing with light or no modulation, and layer playing with heavy modulation on top of it.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.L Time: Adjusts the length of time before the left delay's first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.LFeedback: Controls the number of repeats for the left delay. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.
params.R Time: Adjusts the length of time before the right delay's first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.RFeedback: Controls the number of repeats for the right delay. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the filter modulation applied to the repeats.

params.Delay 1: Adjusts the delay time of Deck 1. Delay 1 can go up to 20 ms and Delay 2 can go up to 200 ms.
params.Delay 2: Adjusts the delay time of Deck 2. Delay 1 can go up to 20 ms and Delay 2 can go up to 200 ms.
params.WowFlutr1: Controls how much warbly tape sound is heard from Deck 1.
params.WowFlutr2: Controls how much warbly tape sound is heard from Deck 2.
params.Saturate1: Adds analog tape saturation to Deck 1 and at high enough settings, distortion. At lower settings, it's great for simply warming up a tone.
params.Saturate2: Adds analog tape saturation to Deck 2 and at high enough settings, distortion. At lower settings, it's great for simply warming up a tone.
params.Deck 1 Vol: Sets the level of Deck 1. Deck 2 is a bit lower than Deck 1 by default.
params.Deck 2 Vol: Sets the level of Deck 2. Deck 2 is a bit lower than Deck 1 by default.
params.Deck 2 Pol: When set to "Invert," inverts the polarity of Deck 2.
params.Mod Rate: Controls the rate or speed of modulation applied to Deck 2.
params.Mod Depth: Controls the depth or amount of modulation applied to Deck 2.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.TapeSpeed: Changes both the rate of the modulation applied by the WowFluttr control and the filtering response of the analog tape emulation.
params.Texture: Adjusts the amount of the NAB tape EQ in the simulated tape path. When Saturation is set to 0.0, the texture is invisible. When Saturation is turned up, the texture will affect the tightness (or looseness) of the distortion.
params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter to the decks, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter to the decks, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.
params.EnvThresh: Sets the level above which engages the envelope. When on, picking harder can impart very slight pitch fluctuations by tweaking Deck 2's delay. Subtle, but fun.

params.Delay 1: Adjusts the delay time of Deck 1. Delay 1 can go up to 20 ms and Delay 2 can go up to 200 ms.
params.Delay 2: Adjusts the delay time of Deck 2. Delay 1 can go up to 20 ms and Delay 2 can go up to 200 ms.
params.WowFlutr1: Controls how much warbly tape sound is heard from Deck 1.
params.WowFlutr2: Controls how much warbly tape sound is heard from Deck 2.
params.Saturate1: Adds analog tape saturation to Deck 1 and at high enough settings, distortion. At lower settings, it's great for simply warming up a tone.
params.Saturate2: Adds analog tape saturation to Deck 2 and at high enough settings, distortion. At lower settings, it's great for simply warming up a tone.
params.Deck 1 Vol: Sets the level of Deck 1. Deck 2 is a bit lower than Deck 1 by default.
params.Deck 2 Vol: Sets the level of Deck 2. Deck 2 is a bit lower than Deck 1 by default.
params.Deck 2 Pol: When set to "Invert," inverts the polarity of Deck 2.
params.Mod Rate: Controls the rate or speed of modulation applied to Deck 2.
params.Mod Depth: Controls the depth or amount of modulation applied to Deck 2.

params.Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the pitch modulation applied to the repeats.

params.Time: Adjusts the delay time of tape head 3. Cosmos Echo has a maximum delay length of 2 seconds, with the delay time divided evenly between the 3 tape heads. So if Time is set to 1.500 seconds, tape head 1's time is 500 ms (1500 / 3 = 500). When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Ramp: Controls how fast the tape speed changes when adjusting the Time parameter. Ramp has no affect on the signal except when Time is being adjusted.
params.Feedback: Controls the number of delay repeats for all four tape heads. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the Delay may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).
params.Wow Fluttr: Controls how much warbly tape sound is heard. Lower values result in the sound of a tape echo in pristine condition; higher values result in the sound of a tape echo that may have seen one too many trips in the back of a van.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.Headroom: Some delay units' internal signal paths exhibit a bit of grit, especially when placed after a high-gain amp block. Negative values increase the perceived amount of grit; positive values clean things up a bit.
params.Mode: Determines which combination of up to three tape heads is active. Head 3 reflects the full delay time (set with the Time parameter). Head 1's time is 1/3 that of Head 3, and Head 2's time is 2/3 that of Head 3.
params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ applied to the repeats.
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ applied to the repeats.
params.FB Tone: Determines how the frequency bandwidth of the repeats changes over time, particularly when Feedback is set high. Lower values gradually roll off more of the highs, approximating the behavior of older tape. Higher values maintain more high end for more repeats, like new tape fresh out of the box.
params.Splice: Controls the level of the tape splice. Like the original unit, Cosmos Echo uses virtual tape with ends that are spliced together. When this spliced area of the tape travels over the heads, a slight warble can be heard. Time also affects how frequently the tape splice occurs.
params.Dry Thru: When off, the dry signal is routed through the tape delay's circuitry (even with Mix set to 0%), which can add a bit of warmth and grit. When on, the dry signal bypasses the delay's circuitry.

params.Smoothing: Higher values apply smoothing between slices and can give a synth-pad type quality; lower values maintain transients. Or set it just high enough to avoid pops and clicks.
params.Interval 1: Sets the pitch of some repeats, the likelihood of which is determined by the Pitch parameter (from an octave down to an octave up).
params.Interval 2: Sets the pitch of other repeats, the likelihood of which is determined by the Pitch parameter (from an octave down to an octave up).

params.Key: Along with Scale, specifies the scale reference for V1 Shift and V2 Shift values. For example, if you choose D Minor and then PLAY IN D MINOR (Harmony Delay can't fix bad notes), V1 Shift and V2 Shift will always shift your repeats to pitches in that scale.

params.V1 Shift: Selects voice/harmony 1's note in the specified Key. For example, if Key is set to "D" and Scale is set to "Minor" (which I always find is the saddest of all keys), setting V1 Shift to +3 will repeat an F (or the third note above D in the D minor scale).
params.V1 Level: Controls the level of the voice/harmony 1 repeats.
params.V1 Pan: Controls the panning of the voice/harmony 1 repeats between the left and right channels.
params.V2 Shift: Selects voice/harmony 2's note in the specified Key. For example, if Key is set to "D" and Scale is set to "Minor" (which I always find is the saddest of all keys), setting V2 Shift to -2 will repeat a Bb (or the second note below D in the D minor scale).

params.V2 Pan: Controls the panning of the voice/harmony 2 repeats between the left and right channels.

The higher the value, the more EQ is applied at the shift end points; when set to 0.0, no compensation EQ is applied.

params.First: Determines the length of the repeats at the beginning of the sequence, that is, the length of repeated audio when the block is first engaged. When set to note values, First (Time) follows the system tempo.
params.Last: Determines the length of the repeats at the end of the sequence. If shorter than the First step's time, the sequence will get shorter; if longer than the First step's time, the sequence will get longer. If First and Last are the same time, the sequence length remains constant. When set to note values, Last (Time) follows the system tempo.
params.Steps: Determines how many steps there are in the sequence (1 to 50), with steps in the middle interpolating repeat length, speed/pitch, and/or filter cutoff. For example, if your first step is 100 ms and your last step is 500 ms, each successive step in the sequence will interpolate between 100 ms and 500 ms.
params.Direction: Determines the direction of the repeats. "Forward" makes each repeat play back normally. "Reverse" causes repeats to play back in reverse. "Fwd/Rev" alternates between forward and reverse.
params.Boomerang: When on, the sequence plays forward, then backward, then forward again, etc. When off, the end of the sequence repeats indefinitely.
params.Operation: Determines what happens to your signal when Tesselator is turned on. When set to "Mute All," THE ENTIRE PATH IS MUTED. When set to "Dry Kill," only the effected signal is heard. When set to "Normal," both the effected and dry signals are heard. TIP: With Tesselator on a parallel path, assign a second stomp switch to toggle between Mute All and Dry Kill.
params.Ramp: Determines whether any speed/pitch changes across the sequence reference a static or semitone value. "Speed" sets the target speed of the last step; use the Speed parameter to set the specific value (0% ~ 200% speed). "Pitch" sets the target pitch of the last step; use the Pitch parameter to set the value (-12 ~ +12 semitones).
params.Speed: Sets the speed for the last step in the sequence. For example, if set to 200%, the last step's speed will be twice as fast as the first step and if set to 0%, the last step will appear to stop completely, almost like a glitchy tape stop effect. Disabled unless Ramp is set to "Speed."
params.Pitch: Sets the pitch shift for the last step in semitones. For example, if set to -12, the last step will be an octave lower than the first step. Disabled unless Ramp is set to "Pitch."
params.HP Filter: Controls the high-pass (low cut) filter frequency for the last step. For example, if set to a higher value, each successive step will filter out more bass until the last step of the sequence.
params.LP Filter: Controls the low-pass (high cut) filter frequency for the last step. For example, if set to a lower value, each successive step will filter out more treble until the last step of the sequence.
params.FX Level: Controls the level of the effected signal.

params.Step Time: Sets the time between steps. The total delay time is Time x Steps, so [Time: 1/16 x Steps: 8] is a 1/2-note. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.
params.Feedback: Controls the overall number of repeats heard for the entire sequence. If you want to hear all fills in the sequence only once, set to 0%.
params.Steps: Determines the number of steps in the sequence, from 1 to 16.
params.Fill: Controls the number of active taps (from 1 to 16), whose spacing is set by Euclidean algorithms. If Fill is higher than Steps, the extra taps are ignored.
params.Rotate: Rotates all fills forward by the same amount (0-15). Used if you like the sound of a repeat pattern but want the fills and gaps shifted forward.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the delay sequence and the dry signal. At 0%, no delay sequence is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter to the fills, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter to the fills, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Fdbk Gain: Controls the amount of feedback. At higher settings, can easily overwhelm your guitar signal; at lower settings, the feedback can better "sit" between chords. WARNING! Be careful, as this effect can quickly go off the rails, just like real feedback. Consider assigning it to a momentary stomp so feedback only appears while you hold the switch.
params.Fdbk Type: Determines the type of the feedback generated. For Mid to Low (or High to Low), feedback starts on the highest harmonic below 500 Hz (or 1200 Hz) and descends to lower harmonics. Rndm Onset harmonics are selected randomly every time a new note or chord is detected. Rndm Trigger harmonics are selected randomly every time Retrigger is set to "Trigger."
params.Attack: Controls how quickly feedback appears.
params.Release: Controls how quickly each harmonic dies out or transitions to a different one. At higher values, you may hear more than one harmonic as they transition.
params.Dry Kill: Determines what happens to the dry signal: Off-The dry signal is controlled by the Dry Level parameter but is unaffected when the block is turned on. On-The dry signal is muted when the block is turned on. Always-The dry signal is muted from the entire path, regardless of whether the block is on or off. Use this setting only when Feedbacker is on a parallel path.
params.Dry Level: Adjusts the amount of dry signal through the Feedbacker block.
params.Reference: Determines which note within a chord is referenced by the feedback. "Lowest" prioritizes a chord's lowest-pitched note while "Loudest" prioritizes the loudest note in the chord.
params.Silence Thr: Adjusts the level threshold above which feedback is generated. Below this level, no feedback is generated.
params.Onset Thr: When Feedback Type is set to Rndm Offset, sets the threshold of onsets (plucks) that cause changes to the feedback note. Lower values increase sensitivity to plucking and strumming and higher values reduce sensitivity.
params.Offset Thr: Rapid drops in the signal level by this amount will quickly kill the feedback to prevent warbling.
params.Retrigger: Meant to be assigned to a Stomp switch. Every time you press the switch, the feedback changes, depending on the type of mode: Mid to Low or High to Low-Feedback descends to lower harmonics. Rndm Trigger or Rndm Offset-Feedback randomly chooses a different harmonic. All other modes-Feedback regenerates at the mode's selected frequency.
params.Trails: Determines whether feedback continues to ring out (for the duration of the Release parameter) after the block is bypassed.

params.Mode: Selects the type of filter effect (Low Pass, Band Pass, or High Pass).
params.FilterGain: Controls the amount of boost or cut applied to the filtered frequencies.
params.Filter Q: Controls the resonance or width of the frequency band affected by the filter.
params.Sens: Determines how Autofilter responds to your playing dynamics. Lower values are less sensitive to pick attack; higher values are more sensitive.
params.Attack: Controls how long it takes for the filter to reach its high frequency (determined by Sensitivity and your playing dynamics) once the transient is detected. Lower values are better for funky rhythmic playing; higher values are better for slow filter sweeps and special effects.
params.Decay: Controls how long it takes for the filter to return to its original cutoff frequency after the Attack stage.
params.Frequency: Sets the initial filter frequency when no input signal is detected.
params.FreqDepth: Sets the amount of frequency change. If FreqDepth's value is lower than Frequency's value, the filter frequency remains static.
params.Direction: Determines whether playing dynamics push the filter frequency higher or lower.
params.Mix: Controls the balance between the filtered and dry signals. At 0%, no filtered signal is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Send: Sets the level of the Send 1 signal. 0.0 dB is unity gain.
params.Return: Sets the level of the Return 1 signal. 0.0 dB is unity gain.
params.Mix: Controls the amount of signal sent through the FX Loop. When connecting time-based pedals like delays or reverbs, it's best to leave the pedal's Mix at 100% and control the amount of the pedal's effect from the FX Loop block's Mix knob; this helps minimize phase issues and latency. For pedals like distortion, fuzz, or compression, it's common to keep the FX Loop's Mix knob at 100% so the entire signal is effected, although parallel processing can be accomplished at lower values.

params.Pad: Applies a pad to the input. Set to "Off/Inst" for guitars and basses with passive pickups. Set to "On/Line" for guitars and basses with loud active pickups or line level products like synths or drum machines. Set to "Global" to follow the Global Settings > Ins/Outs > Instrument In 1 Pad setting, so it doesn't need to be set for every preset.
params.Trim: Sets the Instrument 1 digital input level and is used to compensate for overly soft or loud instruments. IMPORTANT! Setting Trim to a value higher (or lower) than 0.0 dB effectively boosts (or attenuates) your signal into the first block, which may result in a less than accurate response. Or you might like it.
params.Gate: Turns the Input block's built-in noise gate on and off.
params.Threshold: Sets the noise gate's Threshold. The gate "opens" when the signal's level exceeds the Threshold, to let audio pass through. The gate "closes" when the signal's level drops below the Threshold. Adjust Threshold so only softer, unwanted signals (such as noise or hum) are gated.
params.Decay: Controls the length of time it takes for the open noise gate to close once the signal drops below the Threshold. Increase Decay if you want the gate to gradually lower the signal instead of chopping it off abruptly.

params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter, letting you remove all audio below a certain frequency. May be useful in removing undesirable low end rumble.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter, letting you remove all audio above a certain frequency. May be useful in removing high end harshness.
params.Polarity: Inverts the polarity of the signal.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the incoming “dry” signal and the Cab IR-processed “wet” signal. At 0%, no IR is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. Normally, this should be left at 100%.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the IR.
params.Pan: Controls the panning of the IR between the left and right channels. For stereo setups, the Cab block can sound much wider if the two sides are panned opposite of one another ("L 100" and "R 100")
params.Delay: Delays the signal slightly to time-align with the other side of the Cab block (helping to avoid phase issues). It can also be used to purposely impart a bit of phase incoherence or at higher values, increase the Cab block's apparent stereo width. A little goes a long way here.

params.A Level: Adjusts the output level of stereo Path A (upper).
params.A Pan: Adjusts the left/right stereo balance of Path A (upper). When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through.
params.B Level: Adjusts the output level of stereo Path B (lower).
params.B Pan: Adjusts the left/right stereo balance of Path B (lower). When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through.
params.B Polarity: Inverts the polarity of Path B. Typically, this should be set to "Normal."
params.Level: Sets the overall output level of the Merge block.

params.Rate: Controls the speed of the chorus’ low-frequency oscillator (LFO) from slow to fast.
params.Depth: Controls the amplitude of the modulation, from mild to deep.
params.NumVoices: Determines the number of voices in the chorus (2, 3, or 4).
params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter to the chorus, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.
params.High Shelf: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter to the fills, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the chorus effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no chorus effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Mix: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no modulation is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.Headroom: Some chorus pedals' internal signal paths exhibit a bit of grit, especially when placed after a high-gain amp block. Negative values increase the perceived amount of grit; positive values clean things up a bit.

params.Rate: Controls the speed or rate of the chorus/vibrato. When set to note values, Rate follows the system tempo.

params.Speed: Controls the speed or rate of the chorus. When set to note values, Speed follows the system tempo.
params.Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the chorus. Higher values can get into pretty warbly territory, depending on the WavShape value.
params.Predelay: Applies a bit of delay to the affected signal which at higher values, can impart a bit of ADT (Automatic Double Tracking) sound. Most evident when Mix is not maxed out or the Chorus block is on a parallel path.
params.WavShape: Selects one of seven wave shapes for the modulation.
params.Tone: Controls the overall tonal balance of the chorus.
params.Spread: Controls the apparent stereo width of the chorus between the left and right channels.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no modulation is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Rate: Controls the speed or rate of the chorus. Only active when LFO Man is turned on. When set to note values, Rate follows the system tempo.
params.L Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the Left delay channel/chorus circuit 1.
params.C Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the Center delay channel/chorus circuit 2.
params.R Depth: Controls the depth or intensity of the Right delay channel/chorus circuit 3.
params.LFO Prst: When on, engages an "ensemble-style" chorus preset with fixed Rate, L Depth, C Depth, and R Depth.
params.LFO Man: When on, enables control of Rate, L Depth, C Depth, and R Depth. Can be used in conjunction with LFO Prst.
params.L Boost: Adds an enhanced frequency response to the Left delay channel, making it a bit more pronounced.
params.C Boost: Adds an enhanced frequency response to the Center delay channel, making it a bit more pronounced.
params.R Boost: Adds an enhanced frequency response to the Right delay channel, making it a bit more pronounced.
params.Mode: Selects whether Trinity Chorus operates in mono or stereo.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no modulation is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Doubles: Selects the number of additional voices, 1-4.
params.Slop: Controls the apparent tightness or sloppiness of the additional voices. Higher values result in more slop, or more variation between the voices.
params.Sensitivity: Adjusts the Slop parameter's sensitivity to playing dynamics. At higher values, playing harder generates more slop.
params.Dry Level: Controls the level of the dry (uneffected) signal.
params.Wet Level: Controls the level of the wet (effected) signal.

params.Rate: Controls the speed or rate of the flanger. When set to note values, Speed follows the system tempo.
params.Range: Sets the lower limit of the flanger sweep. Higher values result in wider, more dramatic sweeps. When FreezeLFO is on, sweeps the frequency of the comb filter.
params.Color: Controls the intensity of the flanger sweep by increasing feedback. Higher values result in more of that classic "whoosh."
params.FreezeLFO: When on, disables the automatic flanger sweep (LFO), so Rate no longer affects the sound. Adjusting Range then manually sweeps the frequency of the comb filter.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.Headroom: Provides up to 12.0 dB of additional headroom.

params.Speed: Controls the speed or rate of the flanger when Ctl Select is set to "LFO." When Speed is set to note values, it follows the system tempo. Does nothing when Ctl Select is set to "Envelope" or "Manual."
params.Ctl Select: Selects whether the flanger sweep shifts up and down automatically like a traditional flanger ("LFO"), responds to your playing dynamics ("Envelope"), or is adjusted manually from the Manual knob/slider ("Manual").
params.Depth: Controls how wide and dramatic the flanging sweep appears.
params.Manual: Manually controls the flanger sweep when Ctl Select is set to "Manual." Does nothing when Ctl Select is set to "LFO" or "Envelope."
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal.
params.Phasing: Chooses whether the effect produces in-phase flanging (negative values) or out-of-phase flanging (positive values).
params.CV Dyn: Controls how wide the sweep range is based on your playing dynamics when Ctl Select is set to "Envelope." Higher values result in a wider range. Does nothing when Ctl Select is set to "LFO" or "Manual."
params.Max Delay: Sets the longest point of the flanger sweep. Higher values can result in spacey slapback delay and chorus-type sounds.
params.CVTrackng: Selects whether the flanger sweep moves from high to low ("Normal") or from low to high ("Inverted").
params.Env Lag: Delays the flanger sweep slightly when Ctl Select is set to "Envelope." Does nothing when Ctl Select is set to "LFO" or "Manual."
params.Env Input: If your playing dynamics aren't generating the desired flanger sweep range (when Ctl Select is set to "Envelope"), adjust this setting so that your hardest picking triggers the highest point of your ideal sweep. Does nothing when Ctl Select is set to "LFO" or "Manual."
params.CV Decay: Controls the super quick initial sweep down (or sweep up if CVTrackng is set to "Inverted"). x1 is about 0.5 seconds long, x2 is about 1 second, and x4 is about 2 seconds. Does nothing when Ctl Select is set to "LFO" or "Manual."

params.SW1: Enables/disables Mode 1, which has the lowest level of effect intensity. Like the original, multiple modes can be enabled at once.
params.SW2: Enables/disables Mode 2, which has a medium level of effect intensity. Like the original, multiple modes can be enabled at once.
params.SW3: Enables/disables Mode 3, which has a higher level of effect intensity. Like the original, multiple modes can be enabled at once.
params.SW4: Enables/disables Mode 4, which has the highest level of effect intensity. Like the original, multiple modes can be enabled at once.

params.Speed: Controls the speed or rate of the panning. When set to note values, Speed follows the system tempo.

params.Shape: Selects the type of LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) waveform that controls the panning. "Triangle" and "Sine" provide smoother movement between the left and right channels whereas with "Square," the signal instantly jumps back and forth.
params.Vol Sens: Controls the peak follower's input sensitivity. Higher values cause the input signal to generate fast panning, which slows down gradually as the input signal decays.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the panning effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no panning is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.Speed: Controls the speed or rate of the step sequence. When set to note values, Speed follows the system tempo.
params.Step1: Determines the number of pulses in the sequence's first step, with higher values resulting in progressively shorter and faster tremolo pulses. "Mute" mutes the signal and "Full" bypasses the tremolo for the entirety of the step.
params.Step2: Determines the number of pulses in the sequence's second step, with higher values resulting in progressively shorter and faster tremolo pulses. "Mute" mutes the signal and "Full" bypasses the tremolo for the entirety of the step.
params.Step3: Determines the number of pulses in the sequence's third step, with higher values resulting in progressively shorter and faster tremolo pulses. "Mute" mutes the signal and "Full" bypasses the tremolo for the entirety of the step.
params.Step4: Determines the number of pulses in the sequence's fourth step, with higher values resulting in progressively shorter and faster tremolo pulses. "Mute" mutes the signal and "Full" bypasses the tremolo for the entirety of the step.

params.Saturation: Adds analog tape saturation and at high enough settings, distortion. At lower settings, it's great for simply warming up a tone.
params.Low Cut: Determines the frequency of the Low Cut (High Pass) filter. At higher settings, can provide a lo-fi effect.
params.High Cut: Determines the frequency of the High Cut (Low Pass) filter. At lower settings, can provide the natural high-end roll-off of old tape.
params.TapeSpeed: Changes both the rate of the modulation applied by the WowFluttr control and the filtering response of the analog tape emulation.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.Texture: Controls the amount of the NAB tape EQ in the simulated tape path. When Saturation is set to 0.0, the texture is invisible. When Saturation is turned up, the texture will affect the tightness (or looseness) of the distortion.

params.Frequency: Controls the frequency of the FM (Frequency Modulation).

params.LFO: When on, enables the LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) to modulate the FM and AM frequencies up and down.
params.LFO Rate: Controls the rate or speed of the LFO. When LFO Rate is set to note values, it follows the system tempo. Does nothing if LFO is off.
params.LFO Shape: Controls the wave shape of the LFO. Does nothing if LFO is off.

params.Frequency: Controls the frequency of the FM (Frequency Modulation).
params.AM Freq: Controls the frequency of the AM (Amplitude Modulation).
params.LFO: When on, enables the LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) to modulate the FM and AM frequencies up and down.
params.LFO Rate: Controls the rate or speed of the LFO. When LFO Rate is set to note values, it follows the system tempo. Does nothing if LFO is off.

params.Mix: Controls the blend between the ring modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Shape: Controls the shape of the main oscillator used for the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier. The oscillator is a sine wave at 0.0, a triangle wave at 5.0, and a square wave at 10.0.
params.DutyCycle: Alters the oscillator wave shape in differing ways. For example, when Shape is a triangle wave (5.0), 50% is a normal triangle wave and extreme values warp the wave toward a saw down (0%) or saw up (100%) shape. Or when Shape is a square wave (10.0), 50% is symmetrical and extreme values result in a wave shape that's mostly low (0%) or mostly high (100%).
params.Octave: The frequency of the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. Octave shifts the AM carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 3 octaves up or down.
params.Pitch: The frequency of the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. Pitch shifts the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 12.0 semitones up or down.
params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the ring modulation, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the ring modulation, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.
params.FM Amount: Controls the amount of the FM (Frequency Modulation) modulator applied to the AM carrier. At 0.0, only the AM carrier is applied; at 10.0 the AM carrier is fully modulated by the FM modulator.
params.FM Shape: Controls the shape of the oscillator used for FM of the AM carrier. The oscillator is a sine wave at 0.0, a triangle wave at 5.0, and a square wave at 10.0.
params.FM Duty: Alters the FM oscillator wave shape. 50% is symmetrical and extreme values result in a wave shape that's mostly low (0%) or mostly high (100%).
params.FM Octave: The frequency of the FM carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. FM Octave shifts the FM carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 3 octaves up or down.
params.FM Pitch: The frequency of the FM carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. FM Pitch shifts the FM carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 12.0 semitones up or down.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the ring modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Speed: Selects Slow or Fast rotary speed. When changing values, the rotary speaker speed gradually changes, based on the RampTime value.
params.SlowSpeed: Sets the rotary speed when Speed is set to "Slow." When set to note values, SlowSpeed follows the system tempo.
params.FastSpeed: Sets the rotary speed when Speed is set to "Fast." When set to note values, FastSpeed follows the system tempo.
params.RampTime: Determines how fast the rotary speed changes when Speed is changed from "Slow" to "Fast" or vice versa.
params.Drive: Controls how much of the speaker's internal amp is overdriven. At higher values, the speaker imparts more of a gritty sound.
params.SpkrBlend: Controls how much of the woofer speaker is heard vs. the horn speaker. Normally leave this set to "Equal."
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the rotary effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no rotary effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.Headroom: Provides up to 12.0 dB of additional headroom.

params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter to the speakers, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter to the speakers, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.
params.Wobble: Models how evenly the rotating speaker and its ballast weight are balanced about the axis. At zero, the speaker and ballast are perfectly balanced; as the wobble control is increased, the rotation of the speakers becomes more eccentric.
params.Separation: Adjusts the separation of the stereo field. Practically, this simulates moving the two listening points further apart as the separation knob is increased.
params.Rotor Drift: Adjusts how close the three rotor motors are in sync with each other in speed. As each of the rotors were belt driven, there are often some differences in belt or motor wear, and it creates some subtle modulation effects between the three rotors.
params.Rotor 2 Lvl: Controls the individual volume of the second rotor.
params.Rotor 3 Lvl: Controls the individual volume of the third rotor.

params.Shift Time: Determines how long it takes for the signal to ramp up or down to the set pitch when the block is enabled.
params.ShiftCurve: Determines the trajectory curve of the pitch shift over time. Start Slow values are concave (slower changes to start, speeding up toward the end); Start Fast values are convex (the opposite). At the knob's extremes (Start Slow 5 and Start Fast 5), the pitch will actually overshoot a little before settling on the target pitch.
params.ReturnTime: Determines how long it takes for the signal to return to normal pitch when the block is bypassed.
params.ReturnCurv: Determines the trajectory curve when returning to the original pitch. Start Slow values are concave (slower changes to start, speeding up toward the end); Start Fast values are convex (the opposite). At the knob's extremes (Start Slow 5 and Start Fast 5), the pitch will actually overshoot a little before settling on the original pitch.

params.Drive: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.
params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack.
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack.
params.Master: Controls the Master Volume of the amplifier.
params.Sag: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.
params.Level: Controls the overall level of the Preamp block.
params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.Sag: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.

To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.Drive: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.
params.Bass: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.
params.Mid: Controls the midrange frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.
params.Treble: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.
params.Master: Controls the master volume of the amplifier. It is located between the preamp and power amp and can be used to get more or less power amp distortion. This amp is VERY loud, and if the Master is cranked, the power amp distortion can be pushed into unpleasant territory.
params.Level: Controls the overall level of the Preamp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.
params.Mid Switch: Changes the value of the treble capacitor in the tone stack. When off, the amp has more of a scooped sound; when on, there is a noticeable upper-mid boost.
params.Jazz Rock: Changes the tonestack's wiring, allowing for two totally separate tonal voices. Jazz is quieter with a lower center frequency for the mids. Rock is louder with a more traditional mid frequency center. Tone controls rarely translate well between the Jazz and Rock settings. If a good sound is achieved in one mode, it is not guaranteed that the same settings in the opposite mode will still sound pleasing.
params.OD Switch: Turns the two-gain-stage tube overdrive circuit on and off. This circuit is located AFTER the tone controls and Drive knob. When the overdrive is turned on it's as if third and fourth gain stages are added to the preamp.
params.OD Drive: Controls the amount of drive or saturation in the overdrive circuit. Since the whole overdrive circuit is after the amp's regular Drive and Tone controls, the range of OD Drive will change based on those earlier knob settings.
params.OD Level: Controls the output level of the overdrive circuit.
params.Bright: Engages one of two different values of bright capacitor, and is more pronounced at lower Drive settings. When Drive is at 10.0, Bright is effectively removed from the amp circuit.
params.FET Boost: Provides a 7-9 dB FET (Field Effect Transistor) boost and tweaks the EQ a bit. The result is similar to placing a FET boost pedal before the amp.
params.PAB: Adds a preamp boost between tube stages 1 and 2, but at the expense of removing the tonestack controls from the circuit.
params.Sag: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.
params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.
params.Hum: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.Route To: Determines the amount of the signal sent to Path A (upper) vs. Path B (lower). When set to "Even Split," the signal is split evenly to each path in stereo. Assign this parameter to a Stomp switch to create an A/B toggle switch.

params.Threshold: Determines the signal level above which gets routed to Path B. Playing softer (signal below the Threshold) is routed to Path A; playing louder (signal above the Threshold) is routed to Path B.
params.Attack: Determines how fast the signal is routed to Path B once reaching the Threshold.
params.Decay: Determines how fast the signal returns to Path A once it falls below the Threshold.
params.Reverse: When set to "On," reverses the path assignments. (Any signal above the Threshold is sent to Path B, any signal below the Threshold is sent to Path A.)

params.Frequency: Determines the crossover point at which your signal is split into low and high frequencies. Any signal above this frequency is sent to Path A (upper); any signal below this frequency is sent to Path B (lower).
params.Reverse: When set to "On," reverses the path assignments. (Any signal above the crossover frequency is sent to Path B, any signal below the crossover frequency is sent to Path A.)

params.Balance A: Adjusts the left/right stereo balance (pan) of the signal sent to Path A (upper). By default, the signal before the Split > Y block is sent evenly to both Path A and Path B, both in stereo. If you set Balance A to L 100 and Balance B to R 100, the Split > Y block splits the stereo signal into two mono signals--left to Path A and right to Path B.
params.Balance B: Adjusts the left/right stereo balance (pan) of the signal sent to Path B (lower). By default, the signal before the Split > Y block is sent evenly to both Path A and Path B, both in stereo. If you set Balance A to L 100 and Balance B to R 100, the Split > Y block splits the stereo signal into two mono signals--left to Path A and right to Path B.

params.Osc1Wave: Morphs Oscillator 1 from a sine wave (at 0.0) to a triangle wave (at 5.0) to a modified square wave (at 10.0).
params.1DutyCycl: Controls the duty cycle of Oscillator 1. Adjusting Duty Cycle to either extreme increases harmonic content of the waveform.
params.Osc1 Oct: Sets the octave of Oscillator 1, with a 6-octave range.
params.Osc1 Freq: Sets the interval of Oscillator 1, from 1 octave down to 1 octave up, with 0.1 octave resolution.
params.Osc1 Pan: Controls the panning of Oscillator 1 between the left and right channels.
params.Osc2Wave: Morphs Oscillator 2 from a sine wave (at 0.0) to a triangle wave (at 5.0) to a modified square wave (at 10.0).
params.2DutyCycl: Controls the duty cycle of Oscillator 2. Adjusting Duty Cycle to either extreme increases harmonic content of the waveform.
params.Osc2 Oct: Sets the octave of Oscillator 2, with a 6-octave range.
params.Osc2 Freq: Sets the interval of Oscillator 2, from 1 octave down to 1 octave up, with 0.1 octave resolution.
params.Osc2 Pan: Controls the panning of Oscillator 2 between the left and right channels.
params.Osc3Wave: Morphs Oscillator 3 from a sine wave (at 0.0) to a triangle wave (at 5.0) to a modified square wave (at 10.0).
params.3DutyCycl: Controls the duty cycle of Oscillator 3. Adjusting Duty Cycle to either extreme increases harmonic content of the waveform.
params.Osc3 Oct: Sets the octave of Oscillator 3, with a 6-octave range.
params.Osc3 Freq: Sets the interval of Oscillator 3, from 1 octave down to 1 octave up, with 0.1 octave resolution.
params.Osc3 Pan: Controls the panning of Oscillator 3 between the left and right channels.
params.FltPreset: Choose between 4 filter responses to shape the synth.
params.FM 3 > 1: Controls how much of Oscillator 3 is used to modulate Oscillator 1's frequency.
params.Low Cut: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the synth, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.
params.High Cut: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the synth, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.
params.Mix: Controls the blend between the synth and the dry signal. At 0%, no synth is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Gain: Sets the amount of gain. Unity is 0.0 dB. Values above 0.0 dB provide an ultra-transparent boost. A value of -120.0 dB effectively mutes the signal passing though the block.

params.Pan: Controls the balance between the signal's left and right channels. When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through the block; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through the block.

params.Mode: Specifies the type of signal sent to the Stereo Imager block. When set to "Mono In", the signal is collapsed to mono before any stereo processing.
params.Width: Controls the apparent stereo width of the signal. Values greater than 100% increase the signal's apparent stereo width. Values less than 100% narrow the signal's stereo width. At 0%, the signal is collapsed to mono.
params.Pan: Controls the balance between the signal's left and right channels. When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through the block; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through the block.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.Width: Controls the apparent stereo width of the signal. When set to "Center," the signal is collapsed to mono. When set to "Wide,", the signal maintains its stereo width.
params.LR In Swap: When set to "On," swaps the position of left and right channels, so the left signal appears on the right and the right signal appears on the left.
params.Balance: Controls the balance between the signal's left and right channels. When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through the block; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through the block.
params.Level: Sets the overall level of the block.
params.R Polarity: Inverts the polarity of the right signal.
